page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m8.4xlarge is a high-memory virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance provisions 16 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an expansive 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates without hardware GPU acceleration and includes no local bundled storage, requiring persistent workloads to utilize cloud block storage solutions over its 10 Gbps baseline network interface.

The 1:8 resource distribution prioritizes memory density over raw compute, making the instance efficient for workloads that demand significant RAM capacity without requiring high core counts. Because compute allocation is dedicated rather than shared or burstable, execution performance remains stable under continuous operation. The lack of onboard NVMe or SSD storage shifts input/output tasks entirely onto network-attached storage, meaning throughput and I/O latency depend directly on network configuration and block storage performance tiering.

This hardware profile delivers cost efficiency for memory-heavy configurations where standard 1:4 general-purpose instances would force over-provisioning of excess vCPUs merely to obtain adequate RAM. The primary tradeoffs center on the absence of integrated instance storage and the lack of included public IPv4 addresses, which necessitate external configuration for persistent data and external ingress. The instance is suited for in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, relational databases with large working sets, data extraction and ETL processes, and enterprise Java application backends.
